Give your own summary statistics ALIDs

Source: R/alid.R
og_alid.Rd

og_alid() adds an alid column to a data frame of your own summary statistics, so it can be joined to OpenGWAS data, and orients the alleles to match. An ALID is chromosome:position:A1:A2 on GRCh38 (see the vignette on ALIDs).

Usage

og_alid(
  data,
  chromosome = "chromosome",
  position = "position",
  effect_allele = "effect_allele",
  other_allele = "other_allele",
  eaf = "eaf",
  beta = "beta",
  z = "z",
  reference = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

chromosome, position, effect_allele, other_allele

Names of the columns holding the GRCh38 chromosome and position and the two alleles.

eaf, beta, z

Names of the columns holding the effect allele frequency, effect size and z-score. Each is adjusted when swapping alleles if the data has it; a name you give that the data lacks is an error. Give NULL to say the data has no such column. A named column must be numeric. Negating an integer beta or z keeps it integer; 1 - eaf makes an integer eaf double.

reference

NULL (indels get no ALID), "other_allele" or "effect_allele" (that column is always the reference allele), or the name of a column holding each row's reference allele. Used only for indels.

Value

data, with an alid column added. In rows that have an ALID, the chromosome and alleles are normalised and beta, z and eaf adjusted where alleles were swapped; every other row, and every other column, is exactly as given. Each message has a class (opengwasr_alid_swapped, opengwasr_alid_undeclared_reference, opengwasr_alid_unnamed) and a count field.

Details

  • Alleles of one length (SNVs, and substitutions of several bases) are always oriented: they are sorted, so A1 comes first.

  • An indel's ALID puts the GRCh38 reference allele first, which the alleles alone can't say. An indel gets an ALID only if you declare the reference with reference; otherwise its alid is NA, and a message gives the count.

  • Where the effect allele is not A1, the row's alleles are swapped: beta and z are negated and eaf is replaced by 1 - eaf. Only columns the data has are adjusted.

  • Chromosome labels are normalised as the GWAS Stores do (chr prefix removed, 23 to X, M to MT, ...), and alleles are upper-cased.

  • data must not already have an alid column, and no two arguments may name one column.

  • A row that names no variant (a missing chromosome, an allele that is not A, C, G or T, a position that is not a finite positive whole number, or identical alleles) gets alid = NA, and a message gives the count. Its values are left exactly as given.

og_alid() assumes two things it can't check without the reference genome: alleles are on the forward strand, and indels are left-aligned, as in a normalised VCF.

Examples

my_gwas <- data.frame(
  chromosome    = c("16", "chr18", "5", "1"),
  position      = c(53767042, 60161902, 75701728, 827587),
  effect_allele = c("T", "c", "AAAAT", "G"),
  other_allele  = c("C", "T", "A", "GGGGCC"),
  eaf           = c(0.58, 0.24, 0.13, 0.04),
  beta          = c(-0.076, 0.055, -0.025, 0.12)
)
og_alid(my_gwas)
#> ℹ Swapped the alleles of 1 variant to match its ALID: `beta` negated, `eaf`
#>   replaced by 1 - `eaf`.
#> ! 2 indels have no ALID, because no allele is declared the reference. Name it
#>   with `reference`.
#>   chromosome position effect_allele other_allele  eaf   beta            alid
#> 1         16 53767042             C            T 0.42  0.076 16:53767042:C:T
#> 2         18 60161902             C            T 0.24  0.055 18:60161902:C:T
#> 3          5 75701728         AAAAT            A 0.13 -0.025            <NA>
#> 4          1   827587             G       GGGGCC 0.04  0.120            <NA>
og_alid(my_gwas, reference = "other_allele")
#> ℹ Swapped the alleles of 3 variants to match their ALIDs: `beta` negated, `eaf`
#>   replaced by 1 - `eaf`.
#>   chromosome position effect_allele other_allele  eaf   beta               alid
#> 1         16 53767042             C            T 0.42  0.076    16:53767042:C:T
#> 2         18 60161902             C            T 0.24  0.055    18:60161902:C:T
#> 3          5 75701728             A        AAAAT 0.87  0.025 5:75701728:A:AAAAT
#> 4          1   827587        GGGGCC            G 0.96 -0.120  1:827587:GGGGCC:G
